target.title: fix(agents): avoid symlink-follow in auth.json bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a local attacker with write access to the `auth.json` parent directory can redirect the credential store's bootstrap write through a symlink. `AuthStorage` is the default credential backend for every agent session, and on every read, write, OAuth refresh, and login it runs a bootstrap step that creates `auth.json` when it is missing. That bootstrap follows symlinks. If the attacker plants `auth.json` as a symlink to a path they cannot otherwise reach but the app user can write, then whenever `auth.json` is transiently absent (first run, or any delete-then-recreate window) the app creates and truncates the symlink target and `chmod 600`s it, outside the attacker-writable directory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is in `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts`, `FileAuthStorageBackend.ensureFileExists()`:

```ts
private ensureFileExists(): void {
  if (!existsSync(this.authPath)) {
    writeFileSync(this.authPath, "{}", "utf-8");
    chmodSync(this.authPath, 0o600);
  }
}
```

`existsSync` (check), `writeFileSync` (act), and `chmodSync` (act) all dereference symlinks with no `O_NOFOLLOW` guard, and there is a TOCTOU window between the check and the acts. When `auth.json` is a symlink to a missing target, `existsSync` returns false and the subsequent create/truncate/chmod land on the symlink target.

The content-write path in the same class, `replaceAuthFileAtomic()`, already avoids this: it delegates to `replaceFileAtomicSync` (`@openclaw/fs-safe`), which writes a sibling temp file with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` and atomically renames it into place, so it replaces the symlink node itself and never writes through it. PR #88029 introduced that atomic path for crash durability but only routed the persist writes through it; the bootstrap create was left on the raw `writeFileSync`/`chmodSync`.

The fix routes the bootstrap create through the same primitive the class already uses two methods below:

```ts
private ensureFileExists(): void {
  if (!existsSync(this.authPath)) {
    this.replaceAuthFileAtomic("{}");
  }
}
```

`replaceAuthFileAtomic("{}")` writes `{}` at mode `0o600` to a temp file and renames it over `auth.json`. If `auth.json` is a planted symlink, the rename replaces the link node with a real file; the symlink target is never created, truncated, or chmod-ed. Same content and permissions as before, now symlink-safe. `ensureFileExists` is the single bootstrap seam every session funnels through via `withLock`/`withLockAsync`, so fixing it here covers all callers; `InMemoryAuthStorageBackend` has no filesystem and is unaffected. The now-unused `writeFileSync`/`chmodSync` named imports are dropped.

## User Impact

Operators no longer expose an arbitrary-file create/truncate/chmod primitive through the credential store when `auth.json` is absent and its parent directory is writable by another local user. Normal behavior is unchanged: a missing `auth.json` is still created as a `{}` file at mode `0o600`.

## Evidence

Local verification (kept out of the proof fields below):

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.symlink-bootstrap.test.ts src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.test.ts`: 2 files, 3 tests pass. The new regression suite fails on pristine main (`victim exists` reads `true`) and passes with the patch.
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` and `oxfmt --check` on both changed files: clean.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json` and `-p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json`: clean.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: `AuthStorage` bootstrap creates, truncates, and chmods `auth.json`'s symlink target when `auth.json` is a dangling symlink planted by a local attacker with write access to the parent directory.
Real environment tested: the real `AuthStorage` class from `src/agents/sessions/auth-storage.ts` driven via `tsx` against a real on-disk temp directory, on pristine `origin/main` cb7468fc58ace11ebd0d6849216fff73b9d84d9f and on the patched tree, with identical inputs. Nothing stubbed: a real symlink `auth.json -> ../victim-secret.json` is planted, then `AuthStorage.create(authPath)` runs, and the real filesystem outcome is read back with `lstat`/`existsSync`.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: plant `mkdir agent; ln -s ../victim-secret.json agent/auth.json` (dangling target), then `AuthStorage.create(agent/auth.json)`, then read whether the victim target exists and whether `auth.json` is still a symlink.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pristine main cb7468fc58ace11ebd0d6849216fff73b9d84d9f)
victim exists before: false
auth.json is symlink before: true
victim exists after AuthStorage.create: true
victim content written through symlink: "{}"
victim mode: 600
auth.json is symlink after: true
auth.json is regular file after: false

# AFTER (this patch, identical inputs)
victim exists before: false
auth.json is symlink before: true
victim exists after AuthStorage.create: false
victim content written through symlink: "<none>"
victim mode: <none>
auth.json is symlink after: false
auth.json is regular file after: true
```
Observed result after fix: the planted symlink target is never created, truncated, or given mode 600; instead the symlink node is atomically replaced by a real `{}` file in place, so the write no longer escapes the parent directory through the link.
What was not tested: no live multi-process attacker race was staged; the proof plants the symlink deterministically before the bootstrap. Full `pnpm build` was not run (no packaging, dynamic-import, or module-boundary change).
